title: Real Madrid’s Thibaut Courtois sidelined for at least six weeks with thigh injury
content:
Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois is set to miss at least the next six weeks of action due to a thigh injury.

The 33-year-old, who on Wednesday did not expect the issue to be major before tests on Thursday proved otherwise, started Madrid’s Champions League last-16 second leg against Manchester City on Tuesday but was substituted at half-time and replaced by Andriy Lunin.

Madrid confirmed Courtois’ injury on Thursday, with sources briefed on the matter, who spoke to The Athletic on the condition of anonymity, confirming that Courtois is set to be sidelined for six weeks, with some fearing it could be up to eight weeks.

The injury will see him miss both legs of the quarter-final against Bayern Munich in April, but it also places doubt on his participation in the semi-final should Madrid make it to that stage. The injury is believed to be due to overload.

Courtois’ absence comes ahead of the Madrid derby on Sunday. Atletico Madrid are third in La Liga, nine points behind second-placed Madrid, who are four points off of league leaders Barcelona.

Courtois has made 41 appearances in all competitions this season as Madrid’s No 1, a position he has held since signing for the club from Chelsea in 2018. He has kept 16 clean sheets this campaign and has started all but one of the team’s Champions League games.

He has been capped 107 times by Belgium, who are scheduled to play friendlies against the United States and Mexico in the upcoming international break.

Ukraine international Lunin is in line to make his fourth start this season, having started the 4-3 league phase win over Greek side Olympiacos and Copa del Rey matches against Talavera and Albacete.

The 27-year-old has deputised for Courtois on several occasions, notably making 31 appearances during the 2023-24 campaign while the Belgian recovered from severe knee injuries.

Madrid beat City 2-1, winning 5-1 on aggregate and advancing to the quarter-finals, where they will face Bayern over two legs — at the Bernabeu on April 7  and at the Allianz Arena April 15.

Courtois’ injury is a major blow for Real Madrid and yet another sign that something has been amiss for several seasons now with the club’s fitness and medical departments.

Head coach Alvaro Arbeloa, who last week described Courtois at a press conference as “the best goalkeeper in Real Madrid’s history”, picked his team for both matches against City with seven players unavailable through injury: Kylian Mbappe, Eder Militao, Jude Bellingham, Rodrygo, Dani Ceballos, Ferland Mendy and Raul Asencio.

It is a scenario very similar to that Xabi Alonso experienced during his around eight months as Madrid coach, and previously by Carlo Ancelotti.

In a decision initiated by president Florentino Perez, Madrid brought Dr. Niko Mihic and physical trainer Antonio Pintus back into the fold in January to resolve this situation. However, the situation has not changed, and injuries have become a major setback that an increasing number of sources at Valdebebas are citing as the main factor behind the coaches’ difficulties in implementing their game plan.

To soften this blow, the figure of Lunin stands out. The reliable Ukrainian goalkeeper was already key in the second half at the Etihad this week and proved in the 2023–2024 season, when Courtois was out for nine months due to two knee injuries.
